"Whutcha Want?" is a song by American hip-hop artist Nine, released in 1995. It is one of the standout tracks from his debut album *Nine Livez*, which was released the same year. Nine, whose real name is Derrick Keyes, is known for his distinctive, deep voice and gritty lyrical style. 

"Whutcha Want?" was produced by Rob Lewis and became notable for its catchy hook and Nine's unique vocal delivery. The song received significant airplay and contributed to Nine's rise in the hip-hop scene during the mid-90s. The track captures the essence of 90s East Coast hip-hop, characterized by its raw beats and streetwise lyrics.

The music video for "Whutcha Want?" received rotation on music channels like MTV and BET, further increasing the song's popularity. The song and its associated album helped establish Nine as a recognizable figure in the hip-hop industry of that era, although he did not maintain mainstream success in subsequent years.

"Whutcha Want?" continues to be fondly remembered by fans of 90s hip-hop and is often included in classic hip-hop playlists and compilations.
